title: Iron-Rich Enamel: Paradigm Shift in Understanding Enamel of Rodent Teeth
content: Teeth represent a remarkable example of natural composite materials, featuring optimally arranged architectures composed of simple inorganic and organic components. These structures exhibit exceptional physical and mechanical properties. The continuously growing incisors of rodents (Rodentia) demonstrate extraordinary functional and structural adaptations that surpass those of human teeth. Characterized by their distinctive orange-brown coloration, rodent incisors exhibit a unique construction in which enamel selectively covers only the labial side (Figure 1), enabling self-sharpening functionality [1]. Mature enamel comprises approximately 96 wt% elongated hydroxyapatite (HA) crystals, with the remaining fraction consisting of organic material and water [2].
